mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's possession FOR being below the competition neutral mean AND Team B's shots FOR (especially recent) being above the competition neutral mean. Both conditions must hold simultaneously — this is a two-observable joint condition, not a single-observable band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match shots-on-target rises when the possession-deficit of Team A and the shot-volume surplus of Team B are both present together, beyond what either factor alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a team (Team A) structurally concedes possession and faces a high-volume shooting opponent (Team B), the joint combination of Team A's below-average possession share and Team B's elevated shots and shots-on-target production is associated with a higher total shots-on-target volume in the match than either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams simultaneously (Team A possession deficit + Team B shot surplus). It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or opponent-descriptor split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team B's shots-on-target FOR / shots FOR ratio for ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5, and Team A's shots-on-target AGAINST for ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5. Condition on both ratios moving in the same adverse direction (B improving accuracy, A conceding more on target) simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Shots-on-target against Team A rises when Team B's recent shot accuracy is higher than its season average and Team A's recent shots-on-target conceded is higher than its season average — a joint cross-team trend interaction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot accuracy) shows a meaningful upward shift in its recent 5 matches relative to its season-long average, while Team A's shots-on-target allowed has also risen recently. The joint presence of an improving attacking accuracy trend for one team and a worsening defensive shots-on-target concession trend for the other is associated with elevated shots-on-target against Team A.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a non-linear ratio (shots-on-target / shots) for one team combined with a trend-shift comparison for the opposing team's defensive metric. It is not reducible to a single observable or a single coarse band; it requires computing a derived ratio and a cross-team joint trend.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (1) Team A's home corner FOR being elevated relative to its away corner FOR, and (2) Team B's corner FOR ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 being above the competition neutral mean. Both dimensions must be evaluated together: venue-driven uplift for Team A AND opponent corner-generation level for Team B.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match corner volume rises when Team A's home corner uplift is large and Team B's corner-generating tendency is simultaneously above the competition baseline — the two dimensions interact rather than simply add.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks exhibit a strong home/away asymmetry (home mean substantially above away mean), while Team B's corner kicks show a smaller home/away asymmetry. When Team A plays at home against a team that generates above-average corners, the combined corner volume is shaped by the interaction of Team A's home corner uplift and Team B's own corner-generating tendency — a cross-team, two-dimension joint relationship.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions at once: Team A's venue-conditioned corner production AND Team B's corner-generating tendency. The engine covers venue split for one team's own observable, but not the joint interaction of one team's venue asymmetry with the opposing team's own production level.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Use half-level corner data for both teams. Condition on Team A's corner FOR SECOND_HALF > FIRST_HALF and Team B's corner FOR SECOND_HALF > FIRST_HALF simultaneously. Evaluate whether the combined second-half corner volume exceeds what a uniform within-match distribution would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half corner volume is elevated relative to first-half corner volume when both teams individually show a second-half corner bias, and this joint back-loading is greater than either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Corner kick production is asymmetrically distributed across halves for both teams: Team A generates more corners in the second half than the first, while Team B also generates more corners in the second half. The joint within-match half-level distribution of corners — where both teams' second-half corner rates exceed their first-half rates — is associated with a back-loaded corner profile that differs from what full-match averages alone imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly to both teams' corner production simultaneously. The engine covers a single observable's half-level split for one team, but not the joint interaction of both teams' half-level distributions producing a combined within-match regime.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (1) Team A's goals FOR SECOND_HALF being substantially higher than goals FOR FIRST_HALF, and (2) Team B's goals AGAINST SECOND_HALF being higher than goals AGAINST FIRST_HALF. Both half-level asymmetries must point in the same direction (second-half concentration) for the mechanism to activate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume is elevated relative to first-half goal volume when Team A's scoring is back-loaded AND Team B's defensive concession is also back-loaded — the joint alignment amplifies the second-half goal concentration beyond what either team's individual half-split implies.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are heavily back-loaded (second-half goals FOR substantially exceed first-half goals FOR), while Team B concedes more goals in the second half than the first. The joint alignment of Team A's second-half scoring tendency with Team B's second-half defensive vulnerability — both measured at the half level — is associated with a disproportionate concentration of goals in the second half of this match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on within-match half-level goal distributions for two different teams (Team A's scoring half-split and Team B's conceding half-split), and testing whether their joint alignment produces a non-additive concentration effect. This is not reducible to a single observable's half-level split for one team.
